mainArticle.title: The Complete Guide to Deploying Full-Stack Applications
mainArticle.description: Comprehensive guide covering Docker, CI/CD pipelines, cloud deployment, and production monitoring

content.markdown:
# The Complete Guide to Deploying Full-Stack Applications Building an app is only half the battle. Getting it reliably deployed, monitored, and continuously updated is what separates hobby projects from production-grade software. This guide walks you through the entire deployment pipeline. ## Why CI/CD Matters - **Speed**: Ship features faster with automated pipelines - **Reliability**: Automated tests catch bugs before production - **Consistency**: Every deployment follows the same process - **Rollback**: Quickly revert if something goes wrong - **Confidence**: Deploy on Friday without fear ## Docker Fundamentals Docker packages your app and its dependencies into a portable container. ### Dockerfile for a Next.js App ```dockerfile # Multi-stage build for smaller images FROM node:20-alpine AS base # Install dependencies FROM base AS deps WORKDIR /app COPY package.json package-lock.json ./ RUN npm ci --only=production # Build the application FROM base AS builder WORKDIR /app COPY --from=deps /app/node_modules ./node_modules COPY . . RUN npm run build # Production image FROM base AS runner WORKDIR /app ENV NODE_ENV=production RUN addgroup --system --gid 1001 nodejs RUN adduser --system --uid 1001 nextjs COPY --from=builder /app/public ./public COPY --from=builder --chown=nextjs:nodejs /app/.next/standalone ./ COPY --from=builder --chown=nextjs:nodejs /app/.next/static ./.next/static USER nextjs EXPOSE 3000 ENV PORT=3000 CMD ["node", "server.js"] ``` ### Docker Compose for Full-Stack ```yaml # docker-compose.yml version: '3.8' services: app: build: . ports: - '3000:3000' environment: - DATABASE_URL=postgresql://user:pass@db:5432/myapp - REDIS_URL=redis://cache:6379 depends_on: - db - cache db: image: postgres:16-alpine volumes: - postgres_data:/var/lib/postgresql/data environment: POSTGRES_USER: user POSTGRES_PASSWORD: pass POSTGRES_DB: myapp cache: image: redis:7-alpine volumes: - redis_data:/data volumes: postgres_data: redis_data: ``` ### Essential Docker Commands ```bash # Build and run docker build -t myapp . docker run -p 3000:3000 myapp # Docker Compose docker compose up -d # Start all services docker compose down # Stop all services docker compose logs -f app # Follow app logs docker compose exec app sh # Shell into container ``` ## CI/CD with GitHub Actions ### Basic CI Pipeline ```yaml # .github/workflows/ci.yml name: CI on: push: branches: [main] pull_request: branches: [main] jobs: test: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v4 - uses: actions/setup-node@v4 with: node-version: 20 cache: 'npm' - run: npm ci - run: npm run lint - run: npm run typecheck - run: npm test -- --coverage - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4 with: name: coverage path: coverage/ ``` ### Full CI/CD Pipeline ```yaml # .github/workflows/deploy.yml name: Deploy on: push: branches: [main] jobs: test: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v4 - uses: actions/setup-node@v4 with: node-version: 20 cache: 'npm' - run: npm ci - run: npm run lint - run: npm run typecheck - run: npm test build: needs: test runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v4 - name: Build Docker image run: docker build -t myapp:${{ github.sha }} . - name: Push to Container Registry run: | echo ${{ secrets.REGISTRY_PASSWORD }} | docker login -u ${{ secrets.REGISTRY_USER }} --password-stdin docker tag myapp:${{ github.sha }} registry.example.com/myapp:${{ github.sha }} docker push registry.example.com/myapp:${{ github.sha }} deploy: needs: build runs-on: ubuntu-latest environment: production steps: - name: Deploy to production run: | # Update the deployment with the new image kubectl set image deployment/myapp \ myapp=registry.example.com/myapp:${{ github.sha }} ``` ## Deploying to Vercel Vercel is optimized for Next.js deployments. ### Setup ```bash # Install Vercel CLI npm install -g vercel # Login and deploy vercel login vercel ``` ### vercel.json Configuration ```json { "buildCommand": "npm run build", "outputDirectory": ".next", "framework": "nextjs", "regions": ["iad1"], "env": { "DATABASE_URL": "@database-url" }, "headers": [ { "source": "/api/(.*)", "headers": [ { "key": "Cache-Control", "value": "no-store" } ] } ] } ``` ### Preview Deployments Every PR automatically gets a preview URL: - Push to a branch - Vercel creates a unique preview URL - Team reviews the live preview - Merge to main triggers production deployment ## Deploying to AWS ### Using AWS Amplify ```yaml # amplify.yml version: 1 frontend: phases: preBuild: commands: - npm ci build: commands: - npm run build artifacts: baseDirectory: .next files: - '**/*' cache: paths: - node_modules/**/* ``` ### Using EC2 with PM2 ```javascript // ecosystem.config.js module.exports = { apps: [{ name: 'myapp', script: 'node_modules/.bin/next', args: 'start', instances: 'max', exec_mode: 'cluster', env: { NODE_ENV: 'production', PORT: 3000, }, }], }; ``` ```bash # On the server pm2 start ecosystem.config.js pm2 save pm2 startup ``` ## Environment Variables Management ```bash # .env.local (never commit!) DATABASE_URL=postgresql://localhost:5432/myapp JWT_SECRET=your-secret-here NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL=http://localhost:3000 # .env.example (commit this) DATABASE_URL=postgresql://localhost:5432/myapp JWT_SECRET= NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL= ``` ### Secrets in CI/CD ```yaml # GitHub Actions - use repository secrets steps: - name: Build env: DATABASE_URL: ${{ secrets.DATABASE_URL }} JWT_SECRET: ${{ secrets.JWT_SECRET }} run: npm run build ``` ## Database Migrations in CI/CD ```yaml # Run migrations before deployment jobs: migrate: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v4 - uses: actions/setup-node@v4 with: node-version: 20 - run: npm ci - name: Run migrations env: DATABASE_URL: ${{ secrets.DATABASE_URL }} run: npx prisma migrate deploy deploy: needs: migrate # ... deployment steps ``` ## Monitoring & Observability ### Health Check Endpoint ```javascript // pages/api/health.js export default async function handler(req, res) { try { // Check database connection await prisma.$queryRaw`SELECT 1`; res.status(200).json({ status: 'healthy', timestamp: new Date().toISOString(), uptime: process.uptime(), version: process.env.APP_VERSION || 'unknown', }); } catch (error) { res.status(503).json({ status: 'unhealthy', error: error.message, }); } } ``` ### Error Tracking ```javascript // Using Sentry import * as Sentry from '@sentry/nextjs'; Sentry.init({ dsn: process.env.SENTRY_DSN, environment: process.env.NODE_ENV, tracesSampleRate: 0.1, // 10% of transactions }); // Automatic error boundary export default function ErrorPage({ error }) { useEffect(() => { Sentry.captureException(error); }, [error]); return

Something went wrong

; } ``` ## Deployment Strategies ### Blue-Green Deployment ``` 1. Blue (current) serves traffic 2. Deploy Green (new version) 3. Test Green environment 4. Switch traffic to Green 5. Keep Blue as rollback ``` ### Rolling Deployment ``` 1. Update instances one at a time 2. Each new instance passes health checks 3. Old instances are drained and removed 4. Zero downtime during the process ``` ### Canary Deployment ``` 1. Deploy new version to 5% of traffic 2. Monitor error rates and performance 3. Gradually increase to 25%, 50%, 100% 4. Rollback if metrics degrade ``` ## Production Checklist ### Before Deploying 1. All tests pass 2. Linting passes 3. Type checking passes 4. Environment variables configured 5. Database migrations ready ### After Deploying 1. Health check endpoint responds 2. Critical user flows work 3. Error tracking active 4. Performance metrics normal 5. Logs streaming correctly ### Security 1. HTTPS enabled 2. Secrets not in code 3. Security headers set 4. CORS configured 5. Rate limiting active ## Conclusion A solid CI/CD pipeline transforms your development workflow. Start simple and add complexity as your needs grow. **Key Takeaways:** 1. Containerize with Docker for consistency 2. Automate testing with GitHub Actions 3. Use preview deployments for code review 4. Manage secrets securely in CI/CD 5. Monitor production with health checks and error tracking 6. Choose deployment strategies based on risk tolerance Ship with confidence!
